title: Big Apple jam sessions and playing with T. Gordon
summary: Late-night jams at New York's Big Apple drew Stuff Smith, Eddie South and Harry James, and Gabriel toured army camps with a Teagarden-like trombonist.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah, I've seen quite a few of them. I never saw any of these women around New Orleans do that, but around New York, Chicago, they could do it. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But, uh. We used to have some sessions, as I started to tell you about that, that's how I run into Stuff Smith, they used to be in there jamming, Eddie South, Shramea Young. Where was this? At the Big Apple in New York. Yeah. They used to come in there around one, two o'clock in the morning. Sometimes we'd have as much as 15, 20 pieces in there. That's what actually ruined music around New York quite a bit. Uh-huh. Back then, thirties and forties, man would hire a piano and drum. Cause he knew so many musicians was gonna come in and sit in, they wouldn't hire anymore. Yeah. And, uh, Harry James and all those fellas used to come up there. They'd have four or five white, maybe about four or five white, everybody in there jamming

That's one thing, uh, with the music, between the musicians there, there's no color. Uh-huh. We was on tour, I remember, with a trombone player, formerly of, who was with, uh, Louis Armstrong, uh, for a while. T. Gordon.

And we played quite a few places together. And, funny thing, we, they had to pay, when we were playing these different army camps, we'd go into officers' quarters and eat, and they made tea garden and he's bad paying.
